subject.title: [Bug] QQ Bot: skill_workshop approval "Allow" button always recorded as rejected

question: Should QQ Bot direct-message approval callbacks rely on exact request-recipient and actor binding, or must they continue requiring an explicit non-wildcard command allowlist?
rationale: The linked PR proposes bypassing command authorization for every non-group callback, but deciding whether direct-chat identity and request binding alone are a sufficient approval boundary requires explicit owner intent.

options.title: Bind to the pending recipient
options.body: Authorize direct callbacks only when account, peer, actor, and pending approval recipient match, while retaining explicit command authorization for groups and mismatches.

options.title: Require explicit allowlists
options.body: Keep all fallback approvals fail-closed unless the actor has an explicit non-wildcard allowFrom entry, accepting the current setup burden for open-DM users.

options.title: Trust every direct callback
options.body: Accept the candidate's blanket non-group bypass and treat delivery into a direct conversation as sufficient authorization.

recommendation.title: Bind to the pending recipient
recommendation.body: Authorize direct callbacks only when account, peer, actor, and pending approval recipient match, while retaining explicit command authorization for groups and mismatches.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the exact implicit fallback authorization gate and is best positioned to clarify its intended direct-message trust boundary.
